title: Opal Health - Escalation Postmortem Follow-up
next_steps: Redwood to share final postmortem write-up and mitigation timeline by 2027-12-03
Schedule 1hr follow-up on 2027-12-06 to review patch rollout metrics
Opal to provide list of top 10 production queries for focused benchmarking
action_items: Carlos Rivera: produce kernel-level profiling from 2027-11-20 incident (due 2027-12-02)
Maya Patel: send SOC2/ISO audit artifacts and exact SSO config docs (due 2027-12-01)
Marcus Chen / Opal: share sample logs and request IDs around 11/20 incident (due 2027-11-30)
Lina Zhou: enable 14-day enhanced tracing on Opal account for next 2 weeks (due 2027-11-30)
summary: Follow-up on the 2027-11-20 production incident where Opal saw increased 95th percentile latency and transient 503s on Redwood Dedicated nodes. Team recapped root cause (KV cache eviction under a bursty seq-length/attention pattern and a misconfigured autoscale cooldown), discussed mitigations already applied (patch to cache eviction heuristics, temporary scaling policy change), and agreed on next steps including deeper kernel profiling, longer tracing retention, and a canary patch rollout schedule.
transcript: 00:00 Maya Patel: Hi everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you all making time. this is the postmortem follow up from the 20th. 00:06 Diane Park: thanks Maya, yeah we want to get this closed out. a few of our execs pinged after the incident so need the timeline and mitigations. 00:15 Carlos Rivera: quick intro, I'm Carlos from Redwood SE; I led the initial triage with Lina and Marcus during the outage. 00:22 Sam Lee: hi, Sam here. we also collected logs, some of which we uploaded to the shared drive link earlier, hope you all saw that. 00:30 Maya Patel: yes saw the artifacts, thanks Sam. so high level we identified two main failure modes: first, the KV cache eviction policy was too aggressive for Opal's bursty large-context workloads; second, the autoscaler cooldown was set to 5m which prevented rapid scale up during the burst. 00:48 Priya Nair: can you explain 'too aggressive' - like evicting active prefixes? that's a security concern if it caused extra retries? 00:56 Carlos Rivera: right so what happened is the continuous batching + prefix caching combined with long-tail seq lengths triggered more frequent cache flushes. the runtime then re-filled cache and caused higher GPU utilization spikes leading to 503s under load. 01:20 Marcus Chen: to add, we saw a correlation between the client-side retry storms and the momentary 95th latency increases; some requests hit a cold KV path. 01:35 Diane Park: we noted retries from our side but we also saw some app-level exponential backoff misconfig; will fix that, but wanted to understand the service side too. 01:45 Carlos Rivera: understood. we pushed a hotfix last week that adjusts the cache eviction threshold and adds a short window for re-use of recently evicted keys to reduce churn. 01:58 Sam Lee: did that require model restart or any infra changes? 02:03 Carlos Rivera: no full model restart; patch is a runtime param change and was applied non-disruptively on Dedicated nodes in our EU cluster. 02:12 Maya Patel: timeline recap: incident 2027-11-20 14:12 UTC, initial mitigation 11/20 15:03, hotfix rolled to EU dedicated 11/24, global rollout planned. 02:25 Priya Nair: what about audit logs? we're documenting for our compliance board—need exact timestamps and who changed what. 02:33 Lina Zhou: Lina here, CSM; we'll export the audit trail and SSO session logs, I'll include the operator IDs and config diffs. 02:41 Marcus Chen: please also include KMS key rotation history, we saw frequent encryption handshakes around the incident window and want to rule out key issues. 02:50 Carlos Rivera: we checked the KMS logs—no key rotations during the incident. I will attach the evidence. 03:00 Diane Park: good. can you expand on the autoscaler behavior? are we hitting a scaling limit? 03:06 Carlos Rivera: currently your Dedicated pool has a burst cap of 8 nodes with a 5m cooldown. during the burst we hit the cap and cooldown prevented quick spin-up; we've recommended raising the burst cap to 12 and lowering cooldown to 90s for the immediate window. 03:25 Sam Lee: would that affect costs a lot? our CFO asked about that. 03:29 Maya Patel: short term bump has modest cost impact; Redwood can enable temporary burst credits while we validate patch to avoid sustained spend. we'll provide a cost delta spreadsheet. 03:41 Priya Nair: what about data residency? any of these changes move data outside EU? 03:45 Carlos Rivera: nothing moves; all operations are within your pinned region and we validated region routing. 03:51 Diane Park: are there any competitors in claims? we had internal talk about maybe moving some traffic to Bedrock for spikes. 03:58 Maya Patel: we heard that. Bedrock could be used for burst fallback but brings model parity and latency tradeoffs; we can set up multi-route fallback but recommend fixing the root cause first. 04:12 Marcus Chen: for root cause, can we get the kernel-level profiling you mentioned? we need to match op timings to our logs. 04:17 Carlos Rivera: yes we are collecting kernel traces and will correlate with request IDs. expect an initial bundle by 2027-12-02. 04:25 Sam Lee: also want to capture top 10 slow queries list– we'll share that today. 04:29 Diane Park: ok next on mitigations: what's the canary plan? 04:33 Maya Patel: plan is canary in non-prod, then EU dedicated 5% traffic for 24h, then 25% for 24h, then full. we will monitor 95th, 99th latency, and error rate. rollback on any 2x spike. 04:50 Priya Nair: curious about tracing retention—we need at least 14 days to debug recurrence. 04:55 Lina Zhou: we can enable 14-day enhanced tracing on your account for two weeks, as a temporary measure. 05:01 Sam Lee: thanks, that's helpful. question about retries—should we change client retry policy? 05:06 Carlos Rivera: yes set a jittered exponential backoff with max attempts 3; reduce client retries will reduce retry storms. we'll share recommended client settings. 05:17 Diane Park: any config we need to change in the SDK? 05:20 Maya Patel: small SDK patch to disable aggressive client-side sync retries; we'll open a PR and share patch notes. 05:28 Marcus Chen: on monitoring, can Redwood emit a custom alert on KV eviction rate and group by model ID so we can set thresholds? 05:36 Carlos Rivera: yes we can add that metric; we'll push a Grafana panel and alert rule you can subscribe to. 05:44 Sam Lee: perfect. 05:46 Maya Patel: moving on to timelines, root-cause doc by 2027-12-03, kernel profile by 2027-12-02, canary start 2027-12-06, final rollback window 2027-12-08, post-canary review 2027-12-09. 06:05 Diane Park: we'll prep exec summary for 12/10 board. 06:09 Priya Nair: one more compliance ask—can you provide a signed statement that no customer data was exfiltrated during the incident? 06:18 Carlos Rivera: yes our security team will provide a statement; Lina will coordinate. 06:23 Lina Zhou: I'll collect the security attestation and share via the secure folder. 06:29 Sam Lee: small note, some hostnames in logs were obfuscated; can we make sure we correlate request ids not just hostnames? 06:36 Carlos Rivera: absolutely, we'll include request-id mapping. 06:40 Diane Park: ok recapping next steps then. 06:44 Maya Patel: recap: 1) Redwood will share final postmortem doc (Maya), 2) kernel profiling and trace bundle (Carlos), 3) enable tracing + audit logs export (Lina), 4) Opal will share slow queries + internal retry configs (Sam/Marcus), 5) schedule follow-up 12/06 (everyone). 07:10 Priya Nair: thanks all, appreciate the responsiveness. 07:14 Maya Patel: thanks team, we'll follow up in email with links and the ask list. meeting adjourned. 07:20 [end of recording]
